lens: Lens 5 - rare-event-relative precision (Sah-Sahasrabudhe-Sawhney, arXiv:2405.20308, read through the Spielman-Teng reader). Dictionary used throughout: the paper's small quantity is p_eps = P(sigma_n(M) <= eps n^{-1/2}) ~ eps with tolerance o(eps); its exact reduction (Lemma 3.2/3.3, secular equation (23), p.7) is p_eps = P(|<v,X>| <= eps n^{-1/2} chi~(X)), the eps appearing as an exact prefactor on one realisation-specific direction v times a POSITIVE O(1) geometry chi~^2 = 1 + sum_i <v_i,X>^2/sigma_i^2 that is dominated by its sqrt(log n) smallest singular directions (Lemma 4.3, p.9); errors are of three classes, e^{-Omega(n)} absolute, O(delta_n eps) relative, eps n^{-Omega(1)} relative (Secs 2, 4, 8, 9). Our small quantity is the Euler-Stein defect delta(0) = e(0) - Lap e(0) of sec_problem Cor. eldan, |delta|_rms = 6.6e-4 against |e| ~ 0.4 on net 0 (sec_measure), needed to ~20% of itself (precision budget of the sst reader, M7: incoherent relative error r on delta adds (r a |delta|)^2 to the 6.6e-9, i.e. +4%/+17%/+39%/+108% at r = 0.1/0.2/0.3/0.5). The exact reduction isolating the small quantity is the Gram theorem (sec_births Thm gram): delta = -<Hess G, Gamma>. New numerical work (Gaussian closure, He-random weights, KH = 40, n = 32..128, L = 4 and 8; scripts and logs in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/lens5/: gram_split.py -> gs_n{32,64,96,128}_L4_s{1,2}.log, gs_n64_L8_s1.log; resample_w1.py -> rs_n48_L4_R24.log; koff_regress2.py) writes the Gram form in first-layer pre-activation-mean space, delta = -tr(S K), and splits it into the part that survives an ensemble replacement of W_1 and the part that does not.

claims.claim: Cleanest formulation of 'compute delta directly': delta(0) = -tr(S K), with S = W_1 W_1^T the realisation's first-layer Gram and K_ab = d^2 G[v_a, v_b] the curvature of the downstream chain G (layers 2..L as a function of the layer-1 surrogate moments theta = (mu, M)) along the per-neuron tilt tangents v_a = d theta/d m_a = (g_a e_a, e_a t_a^T + t_a e_a^T), t_a = T[a,:], T_ab = dM_ab/dm_a of sec_births eq. (slice). Equivalently delta = -sum_{l=2}^{L} J_{L<-l+1}[ <Hess F_l, Gamma_l> ] where Gamma_l = Cov_{xi ~ N(0,I)}( J_{l<-1} dtheta/dm . W_1 xi ) is the covariance of the linear response of the layer-l surrogate moments to a random Gaussian tilt of the input and F_l is the layer-l closure step; and the corrected estimator e - a delta is the chain run with the Ito drift a <Hess F_l, Gamma_l> added at every layer (Eldan's path moved inside the chain).
claims.argument: e(y) = G(theta(W_1 y)) with S fixed, so Hess_y e = W_1^T Hess_m[G o theta] W_1 and Lap_y e = tr(S Hess_m[G o theta]). Hess_m[G o theta] = sum_A d_A G Hess_m theta_A + sum_{AB} d_A d_B G grad_m theta_A grad_m theta_B^T; the first term contributes sum_A d_A G tr(S Hess_m theta_A) = sum_A d_A G Lap_y theta_A = sum_A p_A theta_A d_A G = G = e by the heat-equation/scaling identity of theta_A and Euler's relation (exactly the proof of Thm gram), so e - Lap e = -sum_{ab} S_ab <Hess G, grad_{m_a} theta grad_{m_b} theta^T> = -tr(S K). The layer decomposition is the chain rule for the Hessian of a composition, Hess(F_L o ... o F_2)[u,u] = sum_l J_{L<-l+1} Hess F_l[J_{l<-1}u, J_{l<-1}u], contracted with sum_ab S_ab v_a v_b^T = Cov of v(W_1 xi). CHECKED: max|delta + tr(SK)| = 1.3e-7, 2.2e-7/3.1e-7, 5.1e-7, 5.3e-7 at n = 32, 64 (two seeds), 96, 128 against |delta|_rms = 6.3e-2, 3.1e-2/4.5e-2, 2.5e-2, 2.0e-2 (relative <= 2.6e-5; finite-difference K by 2n^2+1 G evaluations, coordinate Laplacian by 2n+1 chain evaluations; tangent closed forms vs finite differences to 1e-9). This is the analogue of Lemma 3.2: the O(1) identity is removed analytically, so no O(1) difference is ever formed.
claims.consequence_for_system: The Laplacian never needs to be computed as a difference of O(1) quantities: delta is a pure second-order object, the trace of the downstream curvature against the realisation's Gram, and the Euler-Stein correction is a per-layer Ito drift inside the chain. The random normalisation (the paper's chi~, here S and the tangents built from the realisation's W_1) is retained exactly; nothing is averaged. This is the object task #9 should implement.
claims.test: Implement the second-order response propagation (Gamma_l transported layer by layer, <Hess F_l, Gamma_l> pushed to the output) for the Gaussian closure at n = 32, L = 4, seed 1 and compare with -tr(SK) saved in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-thehonesttorus-github-io/9523ef6a-ff73-5ab2-8be3-275df2b5fcc6/scratchpad/wf/lens5/gram_split_n32_L4_s1.npz (keys K, S, delta); agreement to 1e-6 relative is the pass criterion, and its FLOP count against the chain is the cost measurement of claim 7.

claims.claim: The rare-event dictionary. What plays the role of the event of probability eps is the failure of the Euler-Stein identity e = Lap e: eps_ES := |delta|/|e| = 1.6e-3 for the organisers' chain (6.6e-4/0.4) and 2.5e-2 for the Gaussian closure at n = 1024; o(eps) means any error <= 0.2|delta| = 1.3e-4 absolute = 3.3e-4 of |e|; the paper's e^{-Omega(n)} class is float roundoff (1e-15, harmless); its O(delta_n eps) class is everything that acts on an O(1) intermediate and must therefore be bounded relative to delta, not to the intermediate. In the Gram form the cancellation does not disappear but changes shape: the diagonal (hub-local) part has sum_a |S_aa K_aa| / |delta_diag| = 3.2, 5.6-6.6, 6.2, 7.4 at n = 32, 64, 96, 128 (~ n^{0.5}, extrapolating to ~20 at n = 1024) while the off-diagonal part has sum_{a != b} |S_ab K_ab| / |delta_off| = 21, 42-46 at n = 32, 64 (~ 0.7 n, ~700 at n = 1024), i.e. the off-diagonal Gram sum retains the full O(1) cancellation of e - Lap e (0.7 n x 0.35 |delta| ~ 0.4 ~ |e|).
claims.argument: Precision budget: least squares for e - a delta gives a = rho err/|delta| = 0.257 (reported 0.255) and residual (1-rho^2) 3.53e-8 = 6.6e-9 (reported 6.64e-9), exact algebra (sst reader M7, reproduced). Cancellation ratios measured in gram_split.py from the finite-difference K; the n-scalings are fits to four widths and the n = 1024 values are extrapolations. The same sign-balance appears in the spectrum of Q = W_1^T K W_1: positive-eigenvalue mass share 0.44-0.48 at every n and depth (sst reader: 0.38-0.57), so no one-sided bound can be within a factor sum|lambda|/|tr Q| = 6-15 (n <= 96) of delta.
claims.consequence_for_system: Tolerances are set by delta, not by the size of the object being approximated: a closure or compression error that moves an O(1) intermediate by 1e-3 is fatal if coherent, a 1e-15 roundoff is harmless. The Gram form relaxes the tolerance only for the hub-diagonal part (coherent relative accuracy ~1% per term at n = 1024 instead of 3e-4); for the off-diagonal part the coherent tolerance stays at ~3e-4 per term, the same class as the original eps_ES. Incoherent (random-sign, unbiased) errors are tolerated at the 20% level in both parts, because they add a random bilinear form of the same type as delta_off itself (rms adds in quadrature, relative error r).
claims.test: On net 0, no new runs: re-express the existing 2049-run coordinate Laplacian as tr(S H_m) with H_m the pre-activation Hessian (S known) and verify the stated |delta|/|e| and the +17% MSE at r = 0.2 by adding synthetic incoherent noise to the stored delta(0) before fitting a.

claims.claim: The Gram contraction has a realisation-specific part of fixed size: delta_off = -sum_{a != b} S_ab K_ab is 28-46% of delta in rms at every width and depth tested (0.308 at n = 32; 0.459 and 0.304 at n = 64, two seeds; 0.279 at n = 64, L = 8; 0.375 at n = 96; 0.375 at n = 128), does not decay with n, is weakly correlated with the diagonal part (corr 0.12-0.57), and is at most ~25% reproducible from the W_1 ensemble: over 24 resamples of W_1 at fixed deeper weights (n = 48) |mean_{W_1} delta_off|_rms / rms = 0.314 against the null 1/sqrt(24) = 0.204, while delta_diag gives 0.906, delta 0.776 and e 0.9985.
claims.argument: Scaling: K_off/K_diag rms = 0.40, 0.415, 0.412 at n = 32, 64, 64 (constant, not 1/sqrt n), S_ab ~ N(0, 4/n) for a != b (measured |S_off| rms 0.354, 0.250, 0.204, 0.173 vs 2/sqrt n), so delta_off ~ (2/sqrt n) 0.41 K_d n = 0.82 sqrt(n) K_d while delta_diag ~ 2 n K_d / c_diag with c_diag ~ 0.6 sqrt n; the ratio is n-independent, as observed. Ensemble mean: the sign-flip argument S_ab -> -S_ab at fixed K is not exact because K depends on S through T, M_1 and the downstream input, so the mean need not vanish; the measured deterministic fraction sqrt(0.314^2 - 0.204^2) = 0.24 (+-0.1 from R = 24) quantifies this. The fluctuating fraction of delta itself over W_1 is sqrt(1 - 0.776^2) = 0.63 of its rms, versus 5.5% for e: the defect is far more realisation-specific than the estimate it corrects. Caveat: at n = 48 the diagonal S_aa fluctuates with std 0.41 (2 sqrt(2/n)); at n = 1024 that is 0.088, so part of delta_diag's 42% fluctuation would shrink; delta_off's fluctuation is driven by the off-diagonal S and is predicted (previous sentence) to keep its share.
claims.consequence_for_system: 'Gaussian replacement under quasirandomness' of the first layer is inadmissible for delta: replacing S by its ensemble mean 2I gives |delta_mf - delta|/|delta| = 0.26-0.46 (measured), replacing it by diag S leaves a residual 0.29-0.33 after refitting the scalar (corr(delta_diag, delta) = 0.89-0.96); both exceed the 20% tolerance and would add roughly +40% to the corrected MSE (6.6e-9 -> ~9e-9) at best. This is F2/F3 ('realisation-specific, mean-zero over the ensemble, not regenerable from statistics') proved for the defect itself: delta_off is the kernel-vector v of Lemma 3.2 in our setting, a quantity whose ensemble expectation is not a meaningful surrogate.
claims.test: Resample W_1 at n = 96-128 with R = 24 (resample_w1.py, ~30-60 min at 1 thread each) to measure the n-trend of the W_1-fluctuating fraction of delta and delta_off; if the fraction stays >= 0.3 at n = 128 the extrapolation to n = 1024 stands. At full scale the decisive but expensive version is the per-neuron tilt sum delta_diag = -sum_a S_aa K_aa by 2n+1 runs of the chain from layer 2 (tilt m_a by +-h sigma_a), compared with the stored exact delta(0): corr(delta_diag, delta) and the corrected MSE with delta_diag in place of delta.

claims.claim: delta_off is a generic random bilinear form in the realisation's Gram, not a projection onto any O(n^2) pair statistic: the overlap cos(K_off, S) = sqrt(R^2) = 0.014 (n = 64), 0.010 (n = 128) equals the generic level 1/sqrt(n(n-1)) = 0.016, 0.008; the R^2 of K_ab (a != b) on the downstream column overlap (W_2^T W_2)_ab alone or with rho_ab (W_2^T W_2)_ab is 0.0006-0.0035 against noise floors 0.0001-0.0007, and the predicted delta_off from those fits has |pred|/|delta_off| = 0.04-0.12 and corr -0.09 to -0.26; a random permutation of the entries of K_off paired with S reproduces 56-63% of |delta_off| (the expected ~0.71 from loss of symmetry, 2 sum_{a<b} vs sqrt 2); K_off needs n/3 singular values for 90% of its Frobenius energy (10 of 32, 20 of 64).
claims.argument: koff_regress2.py on the saved K (n = 64 seeds 1, 2; n = 128). The fit on rho_ab alone reproduces delta_off to 7-11% with R^2 below the noise floor: this is the tautology that the least-squares projection of K_off onto S IS delta_off / ||S_off||^2 (normal equations), and it says precisely that delta_off is the component of K_off along one direction carrying 1e-4 of its energy. The first version of this regression (koff_regress.py) included S as a regressor and reported corr 1.000 for the same tautological reason; that line is not evidence and was discarded.
claims.consequence_for_system: No mean-field, pair-statistic or low-rank surrogate of the off-diagonal curvature can deliver delta_off: it requires the full K_off paired with the full S, i.e. the second-order response of the downstream chain to every pair of hub tilts, read against the realisation's Gram. The paper's truncation to sqrt(log n) singular directions (Lemma 4.3) has no analogue: K_off is flat-spectrum (rank n/3 for 90% energy), sign-balanced, and its relevant projection is at the noise level of its own energy.
claims.test: Already decisive at n <= 128; the only extension worth running is the shuffle control and cos(K_off, S) at n = 192 (one run of gram_split.py, ~15 min) to confirm the 1/n law of the overlap for one more doubling.

claims.claim: Truncation and probing of the Gram form do not beat the exact coordinate sum. Few-direction truncation: the top-16 |eigenvalues| of Q = W_1^T K W_1 give tr Q within 20% for only 91%, 52-53%, 46%, 24% of outputs at n = 32, 64, 96, 128 (top-4: 28%, 19-22%, 20%, 12%); hub sparsification of the neuron sum: keeping the 50% largest |sum_b S_ab K_ab| rows leaves an error of 12-17% of |delta| at every n (25%: 26-45%). Unbiased probing: the Hutchinson relative noise sqrt2 ||Q||_F/|tr Q| has median 3.66, 4.22-4.64, 4.79, 5.04 (growing ~ n^{0.2}; probes zeta ~ N(0,S) in m-space are identical to input probes), so at n = 1024 (~7-8) a 20% estimate of delta needs S ~ 1400 probes = 2800 chain-from-layer-2 evaluations, against 2n+1 = 2049 for the exact sum.
claims.argument: gram_split.py eigen-decompositions of Q per output; hub sparsification by per-output sorting of row sums; Hutchinson variance 2||Q||_F^2 is exact for Gaussian probes. The paper's truncation works because chi~^2 is positive with terms decaying like 1/i^2 on the rare event (the sst reader verified 91-94% in ell = 3 directions at n = 1000 on the forced event); here the positive-eigenvalue mass share is 0.44-0.48 and the top-k share of tr Q is erratic (IQR of the top-1 share [-1.07, +2.48] at n = 128). The 50% hub sparsification error of 12-17% on delta is milder than F3's 12x on the chain, but each kept K_aa still costs a full second-order response, so it saves at most a factor two.
claims.consequence_for_system: The paper's two structural levers (few singular directions, product decoupling on the event) are absent for delta; its eps-prefactor discipline for unbiased noise transfers (probe noise is relative to delta, a 1e5-1e6 reduction over probing Lap e, where 7e7-3e8 probes were needed) but lands at the same cost as the exact coordinate sum. The symbolic second-order response (claim 1, task #9) remains the only route below O(n) chain evaluations.
claims.test: None cheaper than what was run; the extrapolated Hutchinson ratio at n = 1024 (7-8) could be measured with ~50 moment-space probes of the real chain from layer 2 (100 runs x 41 s) if one wants the exact crossover against 2049.

claims.claim: The companion note's resolvent certificate (C12: ||P - Q||_2^2 <= 2 R_A(h) = -2h Im tau((ih - A)^{-1}) = 2 tau(h^2/(h^2 + A^2))) is not a computable surrogate for delta, in either direction: it is a one-sided bound on the L^2 mass of flipped gates, and for our commuting gates (A = diag(z_a) over the input law) its h -> 0 content is 2 pi h . mean_a f_a(0) = 2 pi h . mean_a phi(alpha_a)/sigma_a, the birth strengths w_a of sec_births eq. (birth) that the chain already holds in closed form; delta is a signed contraction of these births (and of the other closed-form second derivatives, eqs (gate), (birth2)) against a Gram with balanced signs, so any one-sided certificate exceeds |delta| by at least sum|lambda(Q)|/|tr Q| = 6-15 at n <= 96 (extrapolating to ~100 at n = 1024).
claims.argument: h/(h^2 + t^2) -> pi delta_0(t) as h -> 0, so tau(h^2/(h^2 + A^2)) = (1/n) sum_a int f_a(t) h^2/(h^2 + t^2) dt = pi h (1/n) sum_a f_a(0) + O(h^3): the resolvent at scale h is the kink density, the small-ball density at zero (F6), which the Gaussian closure evaluates exactly as phi(alpha)/sigma and which the true law matches to 0.1-0.3% (our-data reader (a); survey reader check B). The companion-verify reader proved C12 and showed the bound is loose by a factor 2 for commuting flips with a continuous density at 0 (and by pi for the resolvent form), tight only for bimodal spectra. delta is not a norm: delta = -tr(SK) with positive-eigenvalue mass share 0.44-0.48 (claim 2), and F6 says the error mechanism is the SIGNED mean shift dm = 1/2 eps sigma phi, not a flipped mass. There is no signed resolvent identity for delta because the Hessian entries of the closure are already explicit Gaussian expectations (Price/Stein), so a resolvent representation would only re-express w_a.
claims.consequence_for_system: C12 can certify an L^2 gate-stability statement for a perturbed chain (e.g. the two-tier compression's effect on the gates), which is a bound on an O(1)-type quantity, not on delta; it offers nothing for computing or bounding the Euler-Stein correction. Drop it from the list of routes to delta.
claims.test: No experiment needed: a surrogate would have to reproduce the sign structure of tr(SK) (positive mass share 0.44-0.48), which a one-sided bound cannot. If one insists: compute 2R_A(h)/(pi h) at layer l on net 0 from the cache (m, sigma) and compare with mean_a w_a; agreement to 1e-3 confirms it is the birth density and nothing more.

claims.claim: Cost structure of computing delta directly. For the Gaussian closure, Gamma_1 = sum_ab S_ab v_a v_b^T is a sum of hub-indexed rank-2 blocks e_a t_a^T + t_a e_a^T (identity leg at the hub a), and the chain's Jacobian injects a new hub block at every layer through the T o delta-m term of the covariance response, so Gamma_l = sum_{sources l' <= l} (cocycle-transported birth blocks); the entries <Hess F_l, Gamma_l> needs are Var(delta m_a), Cov(delta m_a, delta S_ab), Var(delta S_ab), Cov(delta S_aa, delta S_bb), Cov(delta S_aa, delta S_ab), Cov(delta m_a, delta S_bb), each an n^2 array of Hadamard pairings (A o B) C^T of transported legs: the F1 structure at ~12 n^3 per source-age per layer, i.e. the symbolic delta of the Gaussian closure costs about one kappa_3-chain equivalent (~1 B dense float32, ~0.45-1 B two-tier), and its legs coincide with the legs the kappa_3 chain already transports, so the marginal cost on top of kprop3 is the extra pairings (~+50-100%). For kprop3's own delta (the one worth 6.6e-9) the downstream G is the kappa_3 chain, whose Hessian additionally needs Cov(delta kappa_3-slices, delta m), Cov(delta kappa_3, delta S) and Var(delta kappa_3), fourth- and fifth-order pairings of the same legs; estimated 2-5x the chain. Under the score MSE x max(0.1, C/B) a successful symbolic delta on the dense chain gives 6.6e-9 x (2-6) = 1.3e-8-4e-8 against the leaders' 1.5e-8 x 0.105 = 1.6e-9.
claims.argument: The block structure of Gamma_1 is read off the tangent formula (PROVED, it is remark (2) of Thm gram); the injection of new hub blocks per layer follows from delta C'_ab = G_ab (W delta C W^T)_ab + T_ab delta m'_a + T_ba delta m'_b + diagonal terms (eqs (slice), (gate)); the per-layer FLOP count is F1's measured 12 n^3 per source-age, assumed to carry over to the second-order legs (same leg dimensions, two more Hadamard pairings per entry type); the kappa_3-chain multiple is an estimate from the number of additional covariance types, not a count. Remark (3) of Thm gram already states that every needed covariance closes at O(n^3) per layer except Var(delta S_ab), which is the n^4 obstruction unless the CP structure is exploited; the structure above is how it is exploited, at the price of the memory.
claims.consequence_for_system: Computing delta directly is a 1000x reduction over the 2049-run coordinate Laplacian and makes the 6.6e-9 estimator a single program, but it cannot win under the score: it carries the F1 memory a second time (the second variation of a chain has the complexity of the chain's own closure error), and the only chains cheap enough (window-1/2, <= 0.45 B) have a defect that corrects them to 4.8e-7 only (sec_measure: window-one chain + exact delta, corr 0.889, a = 0.482), because the (1 - rho^2) floor needs rho >= 0.9987 from an MSE of 3.7e-6 (sst reader M10). The paper's lesson 'justify every error relative to the event' reads here: measure rho of the short-memory defect before building its symbolic delta; the window-1 measurement is already negative.
claims.test: The n = 32 pilot of claim 1 with a FLOP counter (flopscope on the fnp port) gives the exact cost multiple of the Gaussian-closure delta; for kprop3 the cheapest decisive number is the pending task #13 run (window 2, rank-1 old sources, 2049 chains): if corr(err, delta) < 0.99 the symbolic route for cheap chains is closed regardless of its cost.

claims.claim: The paper's remaining levers have no analogue. (i) Rescaling by exact homogeneity (Lemma 9.2, p.21: the Gaussian small-ball probability is homogeneous in eps, so the quantity is blown up to scale eps_0 = n^{-c} where an absolute n^{-c'} universality error becomes relative): delta is affine, not homogeneous, in the birth amplitude (a first-order chain is linear in its births), and the one exact homogeneity in play, the OU decay (1+tau)^{-p/2} of the kink density along Eldan's path, is already consumed in a = 1/(p+1) (sec_capacity Sec. 3). (ii) Gaussian replacement of an independent component inside the small quantity (Sec. 8, Lemma 8.1, p.17): our input is already Gaussian, the chain's Gaussian closure replaces hidden laws BEFORE the small quantity is extracted (its delta is 15x larger, 1e-2 vs 6.6e-4, and corrects only to 4.35e-7), the kappa_3 chain is the third-order Lindeberg term of Thm 8.4, and claim 3 shows that replacing the first-layer weights by their ensemble destroys 63% of delta.
claims.argument: (i) is the statement that delta_t for births scaled by t is delta_G + t(delta_1 - delta_G) (linearity of the first-order transport in the births), so no scale exists at which delta is both large and exactly proportional to its value at the working scale; the OU homogeneity E phi(alpha_tau) = (2 pi (1+tau))^{-1/2} is what gives a = 1/(p+1), checked three times (0.535/0.500, 0.255/0.257, 0.482). (ii) is claim 3 plus the measured ladder of sec_measure.
claims.consequence_for_system: The structural inventory is complete: of the paper's four moves, 'retain the random normalisation' is exactly what -tr(SK) does (and the chain's conditioning on all weights already did), 'justify errors on the event' is the 20%-of-delta budget with its coherent/incoherent split (claim 2), and 'truncate' and 'replace' are refuted by the sign balance and the realisation-specific 35% (claims 3-5). The problem is rare-event-relative in its tolerances but additive, not multiplicative, in its structure; the paper's estimates do not transfer, its error discipline does.
claims.test: None; (i) is algebra, (ii) is the existing ladder plus the W_1 resample of claim 3.

verdict: The chain's precision problem is rare-event-relative in exactly the paper's sense of tolerances (every O(1) intermediate must be accurate to 0.2|delta| = 1.3e-4 absolute, 3.3e-4 of |e|; roundoff is the harmless e^{-Omega(n)} class), and the Gram theorem is the exact analogue of the paper's secular reduction: delta(0) = -tr(S K), the downstream curvature along per-neuron tilts contracted with the realisation's first-layer Gram, with no O(1) difference ever formed (CHECKED to 2.6e-5 at n = 32-128). But the geometry after the reduction is the opposite of the paper's: tr(SK) is sign-balanced (positive mass 0.44-0.48, flat spectrum, rank n/3), so no truncation to few directions exists; its off-diagonal part is a fixed 28-46% of delta at every n, is a generic random bilinear form in S (overlap at the 1/n noise level, R^2 on pair statistics at the floor, shuffle control 0.56-0.63), is at most ~25% reproducible from the W_1 ensemble, and retains the full O(1) cancellation (sum|terms|/|delta_off| ~ 0.7 n), so no Gaussian/ensemble replacement of the first layer is admissible (loses 26-46% of delta, ~+40% MSE). What transfers is the error discipline: unbiased errors are tolerated at 20%, coherent errors at ~1% (hub-diagonal) or ~3e-4 (off-diagonal) per term; Hutchinson on tr Q is relative to delta (ratio 3.7-5.0, slowly growing) but costs as much as the exact 2n+1 sum. The direct computation of delta is a second-order response chain with the F1 memory (Gamma_l is a sum of cocycle-transported hub blocks; the needed covariances are Hadamard pairings of the same legs the kappa_3 chain transports), costing about one chain-equivalent for the Gaussian closure and an estimated 2-5x for kprop3: a 1000x saving over the coordinate Laplacian and the right engineering target for task #9, but not a route to the 0.1 B floor, because the cheap short-memory chains' defects correlate only 0.889 with their error (floor 4.8e-7). C12's resolvent certificate is the birth density pi h mean(w) in disguise and a one-sided bound; it cannot represent a sign-cancelling trace and is refuted as a surrogate for delta. No estimate of the paper applies; its structure (multiplicative smallness on a positive geometry) is absent here (additive smallness on a cancelling one).
